title: How long does everyone wait?
description:
When processes run **one after another** in the order they arrive (first come, first served, all arriving at time 0), each waits for everyone before it. Write:

```python
def waiting_times(bursts)    # bursts[i] is how long process i needs; returns how long each one waits before starting
def average_wait(bursts)
```

`waiting_times([5, 3, 8])` is `[0, 5, 8]`. Short jobs stuck behind a long one wait a long time, which is one reason schedulers share the CPU in small slices instead.
hints: Each process waits for the total of the bursts before it: keep a running total, record it as the wait, then add this burst to it.
The average is the sum of the waits divided by how many there are.
